title: The URL service
idea: `createUrl` moves code generation and saving into `url.service.js`. It retries when Postgres reports a repeated code, so the controller stays short.
points: The controller validates, calls `createUrl` and replies `201`. It never sees `nanoid` or SQL.
`onConflictDoNothing()` returns no row when the code already exists.
No row means a collision. The loop draws a new code and retries.
After five failed tries it throws; Express 5 forwards it to the error handler.

messages.label: createUrl({ userId, targetUrl })
messages.note: The controller passes plain values. No `req` or `res` crosses this line.

messages.label: INSERT code #1
messages.note: The service draws a code with `nanoid(7)` and inserts it.

messages.label: no row
messages.note: That code exists already. The unique index refuses it, so `onConflictDoNothing()` returns no row.

messages.label: INSERT code #2
messages.note: No row means a collision. The loop draws a fresh code and tries again.

messages.label: row: shortCode
messages.note: This code is free. `returning` sends back the saved `shortCode`.

messages.label: shortCode
messages.note: The service returns the code. The controller replies `201 { shortCode }`.

code.title: createUrl service
code.caption: The service and the slimmer controller come first. A forced collision at the end shows the retry.

walk.text: Plain values in. The optional `makeCode` lets a test choose the codes.
Insert a code. A repeat returns no row; a new code returns its row, and the loop ends.
Give up after five tries and throw, so a broken generator cannot loop forever.
The controller keeps HTTP work only: validate, call the service, reply `201`.
Force a collision: the first code repeats the saved one, so `fresh01` is used.
A generator that always collides reaches the cap and throws.

pitfalls: Cap the retries. Without a limit, a generator that keeps colliding hangs the request.
A failed `createUrl` is a server error. Do not answer `400`; the client did nothing wrong.

quiz.q: The generator hands out three codes in order. What does this print?
quiz.why: The second call draws `aaa` again, so the insert returns no row and the loop draws `bbb`. All three codes are used.

takeaway: The service owns the retry; the controller only maps results to HTTP.

starters: How likely is a collision with 7 characters?
Why is the code generator a parameter?
Why use onConflictDoNothing instead of catching the unique error?
